channel.title: Buying in SeaFlower blog
channel.description: Everything buyers ask about SeaFlower in Bradenton, FL: builders, floor plans, pricing, HOA and CDD fees, location, schools, flood zones and the buying process, from a former builder insider who represents buyers.

item.title: SeaFlower HOA fees explained: what $300.88 a month actually covers, by home type
item.description: The official numbers, what is inside them, why the internet shows five different figures, and the one thing that will change after The Garden Club opens.

item.title: Lake Flores CDD: the official per-lot assessment table and what it means for your tax bill
item.description: The district's own FY2027 numbers by phase and lot width, why Phase 1C costs more, and the answer to 'are CDD fees forever?'

item.title: David Weekley at SeaFlower: Bungalow vs Classic, from a former Weekley operations manager
item.description: Twelve plans on two lot sizes, what each collection is really for, and what I checked on these homes when signing them off was my job.

item.title: Is SeaFlower in a flood zone? FEMA zone, evacuation level and what insurance really costs
item.description: What FEMA's map actually shows for the site, why the flood zone and the evacuation level are different questions, and the three documents to demand for your lot.

item.title: SeaFlower vs Lakewood Ranch: fees, commute, beach distance and what you are really choosing
item.description: I have sold in both. One is finished infrastructure an hour from the sand; the other is the beach side of the county with the amenity center still under construction.

item.title: Do you need a buyer's agent for new construction in Bradenton? What the sales counselor won't tell you
item.description: The on-site consultant is good at the job, and the job is selling the builder's homes. What representation actually does, what it costs, and the registration rule that trips people up.

item.title: Quick move-in or to-be-built at SeaFlower: which is the better deal right now
item.description: Finished inventory carries the discounts and rate buydowns. To-be-built gets you the lot. How to decide, with the September 2026 numbers.

item.title: The honest pros and cons of buying in SeaFlower
item.description: Traffic, density, CDD debt, construction years and one pool for the first phase, weighed against the beach, the design and the sales pace.

item.title: SeaFlower construction timeline: Garden Club, Publix, Village Center, apartments, hotel and Phase Two
item.description: A living page of what is built, what is under construction and what is promised, with dates as published. Updated as milestones land.

item.title: How builder incentives really work at SeaFlower, and how to stack them
item.description: Rate buydowns, closing-cost credits, design credits and lot premiums: the mechanics, the September 2026 offers by builder, and the order to ask in.

item.title: Moving to west Bradenton: living three miles from Anna Maria Island
item.description: What this side of the county is like, the homestead calendar that decides your first tax bill, and the things I tell every relocating buyer from Buffalo.

item.title: SeaFlower market update, September 2026: sales pace, inventory, incentives and what opens next
item.description: The first full year in numbers, what is listed right now by builder, what builders are offering, and what I am watching this fall.
